newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Interbrew asks distributors to halt Burma sales.
newsitem.headline: Interbrew asks distributors to halt Burma sales.

text.p: Belgium's privately owned Interbrew NV, the fourth largest brewer in the world, said on Monday it was asking its independent distributors to stop any possible sales to the Burmese market.
"In doing so Interbrew takes its responsibility as a good international citizen," it said in a statement.
The action followed last week's Belgian media reports that the company was ignoring a call for an economic boycott.
Interbrew said at the time it was not aware there was an economic boycott of Burma or who had proclaimed it.

Earlier this year brewers Heineken and Carlsberg stopped selling beers, and investing, in Burma after calls by human rights groups and Burmese opposition leader and 1991 Nobel Peace Prize winner, Aung San Suu Kyi, for foreign companies to boycott the military dictatorship in Burma.
Interbrew said on Monday it had no investments in Burma and did not intend to invest. It added it had no direct sales there nor did it seek to set up a sales organisation or distribution network.
Interbrew became the world's fourth largest brewer when it bought Canadian brewing group John Labatt Ltd in a $2 billion takeover in July last year.

It has operations in Belgium, Canada, the UK, France, the Netherlands, Hungary, Croatia, Romania, Bulgaria, and the Ukraine, and joint ventures in the U.S., China, the Philippines and the Dominican Republic.
